text:
maya: FYI starting a PRD intake thread for 'incremental streaming + partial response' support on Redwood hosted API. Need problem statement, goals, non-goals, success metrics, and basic acceptance criteria. TL;DR: customers want early token delivery for long responses and the ability to get partial structured outputs as model continues.
jonathan: thanks, maya. quick q — is this primarily latency optimization for user UX or also for cost (early termination)?
maya: both. customer ask from MediaCo: they stream transcripts to UI and want first tokens back within 100ms for snappy feel. Also want to cancel long generations after structured fields arrive to save tokens.
priya: can we get the reporter (MediaCo) use-case doc? need examples of partial structured payloads.
maya: pasted sample from their ops:

```
request: summarize_long_article(stream=true)
response chunk 1: {summary_partial: "Intro: ...", sections: []}
response chunk 2: {summary_partial: "Intro..., Conclusion: ...", sections: ["sec1"]}
```

maya: Problem statement: Redwood currently buffers whole generation for some models and returns only when generation ends -> bad UX for long responses, and prevents token-level savings via early cancel once structured data is complete.
rob: edge case: what about models with reranking/beam search that only emit final tokens after internal scoring? Not all models support stable prefix streaming.
jonathan: good point. We should list compatible model variants and a fallback policy.
simon: non-goals: this PRD won't attempt to make non-streamable closed weights streamable. We'll support streaming for models/runtime paths that already expose partial outputs or can be run with incremental decoding. No attempt to change model architectures.
priya: goals (high level):
- Deliver first token latency <= 150ms p95 for friendly models under standard hosted SLOs.
- Provide a streaming API flag (stream: true) with partial structured payload support and token-level cancel endpoint.
- Emit structured chunks as they become available with schema hints.
- Cost saving: support early-cancel that reduces billed tokens when structure signals completion.

maya: Success metrics:
- UX: p95 time-to-first-byte <= 150ms for 95% of streaming calls in prod after launch.
- Economics: average tokens billed per long-generation customer down by >= 20% within 90 days of adoption.
- Adoption: 10 pilot customers integrated within 3 months.
- Quality: <1% increase in semantic regressions on our eval prompt set for streaming enabled variants.

rob: Acceptance criteria (engineering):
- runtime: expose a streaming socket/HTTP chunked endpoint that forwards partial logits/decoded tokens as soon as available.
- API: documented `stream=true` parameter + `cancel_token` endpoint that can stop generation and return billing delta.
- Backwards compat: non-streaming calls must be unchanged.
- Fallback: if model/runtime can't stream, server returns `stream_unavailable` with suggested model id.

priya: Acceptance criteria (product/legal):
- Analytics: record `ttfb_ms`, `session_cancelled_by_user`, `tokens_billed`, `model_variant` per-call.
- Privacy: ensure partial tokens are covered by existing PII logging rules (don't log raw tokens to data lake).
- SLA: streaming endpoints included in existing uptime SLAs but with clear doc on best-effort p95.

jonathan: Technical risks / edge cases:
- Model variance: some model variants produce unstable prefixes -> may change quality. Need eval harness comparing streamed vs buffered outputs.
- Ordering: ensure chunk ordering across network reconnects.
- Partial JSON/structured outputs: when emitting partial JSON fields, we need a reconciliation strategy (e.g., incremental merge + final delta).
- Billing accuracy when cancel occurs mid-chunk.

maya: Proposed rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (spec + prototype): 2 weeks — internal RFC + prototype on a single verified model (gpt-compat-1-streamable).
- Phase 1 (pilot): 4 weeks — pilot with MediaCo + 2 internal apps, gather metrics and regressions.
- Phase 2 (gradual rollout): 6 weeks — enable in hosted catalog for `streamable` model tag, docs + SDK quickstarts.
- Phase 3 (GA): guardrail + analytics + billing integrations.

priya: Launch criteria (must-haves):
- p95 TTFB <= 150ms on pilot traffic.
- No more than 0.5% regressions in semantic evals for streaming vs buffered baselines.
- Billing correctness validated on synthetic cancels and live pilot.
- Docs + SDKs updated (python/node streaming examples).

rob: Implementation notes for eng-runtime:
- Need to expose tokenized prefix checkpointing (KV cache flush) and chunk emitter hook.
- Consider adding `stream_schema_hint` in request metadata so runtime can prioritize structured field tokens.
- Investigate if quantized runtimes add latency to first token; might need warmup or fastpath.

jonathan: Questions for product/design:
- What should the UI contract for partial structured responses look like? incremental merge vs. replace?
- Do we want a confidence score on partial fields so UI can show progress bar?

maya: design ask: Priya to propose two UI patterns for partial structured results (append vs. replace) and recommend default.
priya: will mock two patterns by EOD Friday and post samples.

product-bot: Reminder: please add this thread to PRD tracker with tag `streaming-partial` and assign owners.
simon: owner suggestion: maya (PM), rob (engineer lead), priya (design), jonathan (data/metrics).
maya: I’ll draft the initial PRD doc from this thread and post a short RFC link next week. If anyone has essential must-haves that I missed, drop them here. :raised_hands:
jonathan: add an eval job comparing: streaming vs buffered, same prompts, measure ROUGE/semantic sim + user-facing acceptance.
rob: also log cases where streamed partials lead to earlier cancels but worse final quality. want a rollback metric.
priya: one more non-goal: we won't support multi-model stitching in v1.
maya: thanks all — capturing action items: 1) priya mocks, 2) rob runtime feasibility spike, 3) jonathan eval harness job, 4) maya PRD draft. Back in a week for RFC review. :calendar:
